climate: Seasons this mild ripen Chardonnay, Merlot, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon and Riesling fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay and Syrah sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Summers are close to rainless. Vines need irrigation or deep soil that stores winter rain, but disease is rare.

soil.rock: Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile. Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely. Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water.
soil.top: The topsoil stores water through dry spells, but stays wet and cold after rain, which slows ripening and can swell the grapes. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.
